parameters.content:
## Watch a Discourse job board and send AI summaries to Telegram

### How it works

This workflow runs on a schedule to check a Discourse job board category for new topics. It fetches the latest job topics, keeps only the topics that have not been processed before, and records them in a Data Table so later runs skip them. For every new topic, it calls the Google Gemini API through an HTTP Request node to produce a short plain-English summary of the job post and a relevance score from 1 to 100 based on keywords you care about. It then combines all summaries for the current run into one digest and sends it to a Telegram chat, so you only need to read one message per run instead of scanning the whole board.

### Setup

- Set the HTTP Request URL to your Discourse community jobs category and add authentication headers if the board requires them.
- Create a Data Table with a topic_id column (text) plus any extra columns like title, url, and first_seen, then select it in the Data Table nodes.
- Create a Google AI Studio API key and save it as a Header Auth credential named for example Gemini Header, with x-goog-api-key as the header name and the key as the value, then select it in the Summarize with Gemini node.
- Create a Telegram bot with BotFather, paste the bot token into a Telegram credential, set your chat ID in the Send Telegram digest node, and activate the workflow.

### Resources

- Data Table with a topic_id column
- Google AI Studio API key (Header Auth)
- Telegram Bot token and chat ID

## Fetch new job posts

The schedule trigger starts the run, the HTTP Request node pulls the latest topics from the Discourse jobs category, and the Code node filters the response down to topics published in the last 48 hours.

## Deduplicate and score

The Check New Topic node passes only topics that are not in the seen-topics Data Table, the upsert node marks them as seen, and the Gemini node summarizes and scores each new post.

## Build and send the digest

The Aggregate node merges all per-topic results into a single item, the Code node formats one readable digest message, and the Telegram node delivers it to your chat.
